faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.a1: A lease takeover is a legal transfer of an existing rental agreement from the current tenant to a new one. The terms of the original lease — rent, deposit, duration — typically stay the same. It's a standard instrument under Polish civil law.
faq.a2: Yes, absolutely. Lease assignment (cesja najmu) is governed by the Polish Civil Code. It requires written consent from all three parties: the current tenant, the new tenant, and the landlord.
faq.a3: Passflat is free: browsing and posting listings (up to 2 active), cost reports, and document templates — no charge.
faq.q4: Do I need the landlord's approval?
faq.a4: Yes, the landlord must consent to the transfer. Most landlords agree because they get a vetted replacement tenant and avoid vacancy — it's a win for everyone.
faq.a5: Tenants anonymously share their monthly costs — rent, utilities, admin fees. Data is aggregated per building so you can see what you'll actually pay before signing a lease.
faq.a6: We use encryption for all data in transit and at rest. Cost reports are anonymized and shown only in aggregated form. We follow a privacy-first approach in compliance with GDPR.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Is a lease takeover legal in Poland?
faq.a1: Yes. A lease takeover (cesja najmu) is a standard legal instrument under Polish civil law. It requires the consent of all parties: the current tenant, the new tenant, and the landlord. Passflat helps you find the match — the legal transfer is between you and the landlord.
faq.q2: What exactly is a lease takeover?
faq.a2: A lease takeover is an amendment to an existing lease agreement where the current tenant transfers their rights and obligations to a new tenant. The terms of the original agreement (rent, period, etc.) typically remain unchanged. The landlord must consent.
faq.q3: Do I need the landlord's consent?
faq.a3: Yes. The landlord must agree to the lease transfer. Most landlords agree because they gain a reliable tenant and avoid vacancy. It's in everyone's interest.
faq.a4: Passflat is free: listings (up to 2 active), cost reports, and document templates — no charge.
faq.a5: We're starting with Warsaw, but the platform is designed for multi-city expansion. Kraków, Wrocław, and other European cities are on our roadmap.
faq.q6: Can I submit cost reports for more than one building?
faq.a6: Have more than one flat? You can add a separate cost report for each building and manage them all from the Cost reports tab in your dashboard.
faq.q7: How accurate is the cost calculator, and where does the estimate come from?
faq.a7: Rent in the calculator comes from the median of tenant reports in the district (or the city median where district data is thin), and utilities from current public Warsaw tariffs (czynsz, heating, electricity, water, garbage, internet). It is a planning estimate, not an exact bill: the real amount depends on the specific building, meters, and season.

about.title: About Passflat
about.subtitle: We're making renting in Poland transparent, fair, and community-driven.

problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: Renting in Poland is broken
problem.p1: Tenants lose deposits when they need to move before the lease ends. There's <howItWorksLink>no easy way to find a replacement</howItWorksLink> — so you either pay a penalty or lose months of rent.
problem.p2: Utility costs are hidden until you sign the lease. You find out about the monthly expenses only after moving in — and by then it's too late.
problem.p3: Agency fees are steep, and foreigners face an even bigger information gap when searching for apartments.
problem.p4: And once a replacement is found, the paperwork begins: a lease takeover, a sublet, a roommate agreement. There are no ready-made templates, lawyers are expensive, and getting the contract wrong is scary.

solution.label: Our Solution
solution.title: A complete rental toolkit built by the community
solution.pillar1Desc: Find a replacement and keep your deposit. Take over someone's lease and skip the agency fee. Lease assignment is a standard legal instrument in Poland — we make it easy.
solution.pillar2Desc: Find a compatible roommate or fill a vacant room. Specify preferences, room type, and per-person costs — so both sides know what to expect.
solution.pillar3Desc: Sublet your apartment for a fixed period while you're away. Set exact dates, total price, and house rules — all in one listing.
solution.pillar4Desc: Community-sourced utility costs. Know exactly what you'll pay for electricity, gas, heating, and water — including periodic recalculations shown as a monthly equivalent — before you sign. And the cost calculator gives a ballpark for any district and size — rent plus utilities — in a couple of clicks.

team.label: Who We Are
team.title: Built by renters, for renters
team.description: We rent in Warsaw ourselves and we've been through all of it — lost deposits, utility bills no one warned us about, a price you only learn after moving in. Passflat grew out of that pain.
team.description2: Passflat is grounded in our own renting experience in Warsaw: moves, agencies, and a lease takeover. Right now that's costs by building, listings (lease takeover, roommate, sublet), and free document templates.

values.label: Our Principles
values.title: Platform rules
values.principle1Desc: We show real numbers — even when they make the market uncomfortable. Every listing includes a full cost breakdown before you contact anyone.
values.principle2Desc: Every cost report is anonymous — it can't be tied to you, and we never sell data to third parties.
values.principle3Desc: Listings and cost data are open to everyone — no registration, no paywall. Add your report to keep the database growing and up to date.
values.principle4Desc: We don't work with agencies and we don't sell your data. Every product decision is made from the tenant's perspective.

costTransparency.title: Cost Transparency
costTransparency.q1: How does the cost database work?
costTransparency.a1: Tenants submit anonymous cost reports for their buildings — including rent, admin fee, electricity, gas, heating, water, and internet. Data is aggregated and displayed per building so future tenants can see what they'll actually pay.
costTransparency.q2: How do I unlock cost data?
costTransparency.a2: Cost data is open to everyone. Add your report — free and forever — to see the detailed breakdown and help the database grow for the whole community.
costTransparency.a3: Yes. Cost data is shown in aggregated form (averages, min/max per building), so individual submissions cannot be identified.
costTransparency.a4: Report your monthly rent, admin fee, and utility costs: electricity, gas, heating, water, and internet. The more complete the report, the more useful it is for the community.

account.title: Account & Privacy
account.q1: How do I create an account?
account.a1: Click "Sign up" and register with email or a Google account. You'll receive a confirmation email to verify your address.
account.q2: How do I delete my account?
account.a2: Go to your dashboard settings and use the "Delete Account" option. Your account will be scheduled for deletion with a 30-day grace period during which you can restore it. After that, all listings are removed and personal data is permanently erased in accordance with GDPR.
account.q3: How is my personal data used?
account.a3: We use your data solely to provide the service — managing listings, sending notifications, and displaying anonymized cost reports. We never sell personal data. See our Privacy Policy for details.

gdprRights.title: Your Data & GDPR
gdprRights.q1: How do I request a copy of my data?
gdprRights.a1: Send an email to contact@passflat.com with the subject "Data Access Request." We will provide a copy of all personal data we hold about you within 30 days, in a structured, machine-readable format.
gdprRights.a2: Under GDPR, you have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict processing, port your data, object to processing, and withdraw consent. For full details, see our Privacy Policy. To exercise any right, contact contact@passflat.com.

payments.title: Payments & Refunds
payments.q1: What can I pay for on Passflat?
payments.a1: Posting a listing is free (up to 2 active listings). Paid services are: extra listings beyond the free limit, promotion to boost a listing's visibility in search results, and time-limited access to the cost-report database. Listings themselves stay free.
payments.q2: When does my paid service start, and can I still cancel?
payments.a2: Paid services are delivered immediately and in full right after payment. Because of this, when you pay you give your express consent to immediate provision — and once the service has been provided you can no longer use the standard 14-day right of withdrawal. You confirm this at checkout when you accept the Terms.
payments.q3: Do you guarantee I'll find a tenant, roommate, or replacement?
payments.a3: No. You pay for the service itself — publication, visibility, or data access — not for a particular result. Passflat doesn't guarantee that you'll find a replacement tenant, a roommate, or a new lease, and not getting a result is not grounds for a refund.
payments.q4: How do I request a refund?
payments.a4: Refunds are handled case by case for genuine issues — for example a duplicate charge, a technical failure that stopped the service from being delivered, or a defective service. Email contact@passflat.com with your account email and the payment reference (you'll find it in your dashboard billing history). Your mandatory consumer rights are always preserved.
payments.q5: Which payment methods can I use?
payments.a5: Payments are processed securely by Stripe. You can pay by card, BLIK, or Przelewy24 (P24). Available methods may vary slightly by device and browser.
payments.q6: Will I get a receipt or invoice?
payments.a6: Yes. Stripe automatically emails a payment receipt to the email address used at checkout. You can also open the receipt anytime from the billing section of your dashboard.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How Passflat collects, uses, and protects your personal data.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.p1: Passflat ("we", "us", "our") is a rental platform (a marketplace of listings, real-cost data from users, and document templates) operated from Warsaw, Poland. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect your personal data when you use our website and services at passflat.com.
intro.p2: We are committed to protecting your privacy in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable Polish data protection laws. By using Passflat, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this policy.

dataCollected.title: Data We Collect
dataCollected.intro: We collect only the data necessary to provide and improve our services:

account.title: Account Data
account.item1: Email address and display name (via email or Google OAuth registration through Supabase Auth)

listings.title: Listing Data
listings.item1: Apartment address (street, building number, district, postal code)
listings.item3: Cost breakdown (rent, admin fee, estimated utilities) and apartment details (area, rooms, amenities, description)

costReports.title: Cost Report Data
costReports.item2: Monthly utility costs (electricity, gas, heating, water, internet) — displayed only in aggregated form
costReports.item3: If you previously submitted cost data through an external form (e.g. an early Google Form), we store the email address you provided solely to link that submission to your account when you later sign in with the same email.

usage.title: Usage & Technical Data
usage.item1: Pages visited, interactions, and feature usage (collected via PostHog and Google Analytics)
usage.item2: IP address, browser type, device information, and operating system (standard server logs)

howWeUse.title: How We Use Your Data
howWeUse.item1: Providing the service: displaying listings, connecting tenants, showing cost reports
howWeUse.item2: Sending notifications: email alerts when someone expresses interest in your listing (via Resend)
howWeUse.item3: Improving the platform: understanding usage patterns, fixing bugs, developing new features
howWeUse.item4: Ensuring security: preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access
howWeUse.noSell: We do NOT sell your personal data to third parties. Ever.

legalBases.title: Legal Bases for Processing (GDPR Art. 6)
legalBases.contract: Contract performance (Art. 6(1)(b)) — processing necessary to provide the service, including displaying listings, tenant matching, and cost reports.
legalBases.legitimateInterest: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) — processing for analytics, platform security, fraud prevention, and platform improvement.
legalBases.consent: Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) — processing for analytics cookies (PostHog) and marketing communications, which you can withdraw at any time.

imported.title: Imported cost reports
imported.description: Some early cost reports were collected via a Google Form and are stored anonymized under a system placeholder. When you log in with the email used for that submission, we automatically associate those reports with your account and grant you contributor access. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) in maintaining contributors' access to their own submissions; you can request deletion at any time.

dataSharing.title: Data Sharing
dataSharing.intro: We share data only in the following, limited circumstances:
dataSharing.item1: Cost reports are displayed in aggregated, anonymized form
dataSharing.item2: Listing contact details are shared only with users who express interest through the platform

processors.title: Data Processors
processors.vercel: Vercel — website hosting and serverless functions
processors.stripe: Stripe — payment processing for promoted listings
processors.google: Google Places API — address autocomplete (address data only)
processors.mapbox: Mapbox — map rendering (no personal data shared)
processors.googleAnalytics: Google Analytics 4 — web traffic/audience analytics (consent-based, opt-in via cookie banner)
processors.deepl: DeepL — automated translation of listing content (EU-based, Germany)

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.account: Account data: retained until you delete your account
retention.listings: Listings: active for 60 days, then archived for 30 days before deletion
retention.costReports: Cost reports: retained indefinitely in anonymized, aggregated form. Once anonymized, this data is no longer personal data under GDPR (Recital 26) and is maintained to support the community database
retention.importedEmail: Email addresses from imported submissions are retained until the submission is claimed at login or until you request removal.

rights.title: Your Rights (GDPR)
rights.intro: Under the General Data Protection Regulation, you have the following rights:
rights.access: Right of access — request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
rights.rectification: Right to rectification — correct inaccurate or incomplete data
rights.erasure: Right to erasure — request deletion of your personal data ("right to be forgotten")
rights.portability: Right to data portability — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
rights.objection: Right to object — object to processing based on legitimate interest
rights.withdrawConsent: Right to withdraw consent — withdraw consent at any time where processing is based on consent
rights.restriction: Right to restriction — request restriction of processing of your personal data in certain circumstances (e.g., while we verify the accuracy of your data)
rights.howToExercise: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at contact@passflat.com. We will respond within 30 days as required by GDPR.
rights.complaint: Right to lodge a complaint — if you believe your data protection rights have been violated, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych, UODO), ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warszawa, Poland. Website: uodo.gov.pl

transfers.title: Cross-Border Data Transfers
transfers.description: Some of our data processors are located outside the European Union / European Economic Area (EU/EEA). When your data is transferred outside the EU/EEA, we ensure appropriate safeguards are in place, including Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission, or adequacy decisions.
transfers.processors: The following processors may process data outside the EU/EEA: Vercel (US), Resend (US), Stripe (EU and US), Google (US, covering both Places API and Google Analytics), and Mapbox (US) — all operating under Standard Contractual Clauses. Supabase and PostHog data locations depend on instance configuration. DeepL is EU-based (Germany).

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: We use a minimal set of cookies:
cookies.essential: Essential cookies: authentication session tokens (required for the service to work)
cookies.analytics: Analytics cookies: PostHog and Google Analytics (optional — you can opt out via browser settings or our cookie banner)
cookies.phPurpose: PostHog product analytics and feature flags
cookies.gaPurpose: Google Analytics — traffic and audience measurement

automated.title: Automated Decision-Making
automated.description: Passflat does not engage in automated individual decision-making or profiling as defined by GDPR Art. 22. Listing rankings are based solely on recency, with promoted listings displayed at the top as a paid feature.

children.title: Children's Data
children.description: Passflat is not intended for persons under 18 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal data from minors. If we become aware that we have collected data from a person under 18, we will take steps to delete that data promptly.

breach.title: Data Breach Notification
breach.description: In the event of a personal data breach that poses a risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO) within 72 hours as required by GDPR Art. 33.
breach.notification: If a breach poses a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will also notify you directly without undue delay, providing information about the nature of the breach and recommended protective measures.

dpo.title: Data Protection Officer
dpo.description: We have assessed the need for a Data Protection Officer (DPO) under GDPR Art. 37 and determined that appointment is not currently required given the nature and scale of our data processing activities. For any data protection inquiries, contact us at contact@passflat.com.

contact.title: Data Controller & Contact
contact.text: For privacy questions or to exercise your GDPR rights, contact our data protection team:

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.text: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. We will notify registered users of significant changes via email. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page indicates when the policy was last revised.

termsPage.title: Terms of Service
termsPage.subtitle: Rules and guidelines for using the Passflat platform.

acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
acceptance.p1: By using Passflat (passflat.com), you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the platform.
acceptance.p2: These terms apply to all users of the platform, including tenants listing apartments, tenants searching for apartments, and users submitting cost reports.

service.title: 2. Service Description
service.item1: Passflat is a platform connecting tenants for lease takeovers — helping current tenants find replacements and new tenants find apartments.
service.item2: Passflat provides a community-sourced cost database where tenants share real utility costs to help others make informed decisions.
service.item3: Passflat is NOT a real estate agency, property manager, or party to any lease agreement. We facilitate connections between tenants — any legal arrangements are between the involved parties.
service.item4: Passflat provides a rent cost calculator — an indicative estimate of monthly costs (rent plus utilities) based on public Warsaw tariffs and community report medians.

accounts.title: 3. User Accounts
accounts.item1: You must be at least 18 years old to create an account and use Passflat.
accounts.item2: You may only create one account. Duplicate accounts may be removed.
accounts.item3: You are responsible for the security of your login credentials and for all activity on your account.
accounts.item4: We reserve the right to suspend or delete accounts that violate these terms or engage in abusive behavior.

listingRules.title: 4. Listing Rules
listingRules.intro: When posting a listing on Passflat, you agree to the following:
listingRules.item1: Listings must be for real, currently available apartments that you have the right to offer for lease takeover.
listingRules.item2: You must be the current tenant of the apartment or have explicit authorization from the tenant to post the listing.
listingRules.item3: Cost information (rent, admin fee, utilities) must be accurate and reflect actual monthly expenses.
listingRules.item4: Listings must not contain discriminatory, misleading, offensive, or illegal content.
listingRules.item5: Passflat reserves the right to remove any listing that violates these rules without prior notice.
listingRules.item6: Listings expire automatically after 60 days. You can renew or close them at any time from your dashboard.

costReports.title: 5. Cost Reports
costReports.item1: Cost reports must reflect real costs from your personal experience as a tenant in the reported building.
costReports.item2: Submitting false or deliberately misleading cost data may result in account removal and deletion of all reports.
costReports.item3: Cost reports are displayed in anonymized, aggregated form.

payments.title: 6. Payments
payments.p1: Passflat offers the following paid services: extra listings (beyond the 2 free active listings), promoted listings (boosted visibility in search results), and time-limited access to the cost report database. All payments are securely processed via Stripe. Prices are shown in PLN.
payments.immediate: Paid services are digital services provided immediately and in full right after payment. By purchasing or activating a paid service, you give your express consent to its immediate provision and acknowledge that, once the service has been provided, you lose your statutory 14-day right of withdrawal (see Section 9). You confirm this consent at checkout when you accept these Terms.
payments.serviceOutcome: The paid product is the service itself — the publication of a listing, increased visibility/promotion, or access to the cost-data database — delivered immediately and in full. Passflat does not guarantee any particular outcome, such as finding a replacement tenant, a roommate, or a new lease. The absence of such a result is not a defect in the service and is not grounds for a refund.
payments.refunds: Refunds are granted at Passflat's discretion in cases of genuine issues, such as a duplicate charge, a technical failure that prevented the service from being delivered, or a defective service. Your mandatory consumer rights remain unaffected. For refund requests, contact contact@passflat.com.

liability.title: 7. Limitation of Liability
liability.item1: Passflat is a platform with listings, user-submitted cost data, and document templates. We do not verify apartments, conduct property inspections, or guarantee the accuracy of user-submitted information (including cost reports). Document templates are basic samples and do not constitute legal advice.
liability.item2: Users are solely responsible for verifying listing information, conducting viewings, and entering into legal agreements (amendments, lease assignments) with landlords and other tenants.
liability.item3: Passflat is not liable for any disputes, losses, or damages arising from transactions or interactions between users or between users and landlords.
liability.item4: The cost calculator provides an approximate estimate based on public tariffs and averaged community data. It is not financial, legal, or tax advice, nor a guarantee of your actual bills; real costs depend on the specific building, meters, tariff plan, and season. Do not rely on it as the sole basis for decisions — verify terms with the landlord and service providers.

ip.title: 8. Intellectual Property
ip.p1: The Passflat platform, including its design, code, branding, and content (excluding user-generated content), is the intellectual property of Passflat.
ip.p2: By posting content on Passflat (listings, photos, cost reports), you grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide license to display and distribute that content on the platform for the purpose of providing the service.

withdrawal.title: 9. Right of Withdrawal
withdrawal.p1: As a consumer, you generally have the right to withdraw from a distance contract for digital services (such as extra listings, promoted listings, or cost report access) within 14 days, without giving any reason. The withdrawal period expires 14 days after the day the contract is concluded. To meet the deadline, it is enough to send your statement before the period expires.
withdrawal.p2: However, the right of withdrawal does not apply where the service has been fully performed with your prior express consent and your acknowledgment that you would lose the right of withdrawal once the contract was fully performed (Art. 38(1)(13) of the Polish Consumer Rights Act / Art. 16(m) of Directive 2011/83/EU). Because Passflat's paid services are provided immediately and in full upon payment, by purchasing you give this consent and lose the right of withdrawal once the service has been provided.
withdrawal.p3: To exercise the right of withdrawal where it applies, send an unequivocal statement (for example, a letter by post or an email) to contact@passflat.com, stating your account email and order details. You may use the model form below, but it is not obligatory. We will process any refund due without undue delay and within 14 days of receiving your statement.

dsa.title: 10. Digital Services Act
dsa.intro: In accordance with the EU Digital Services Act (Regulation 2022/2065), we provide the following transparency information:
dsa.removalIntro: Listings may be removed or restricted if they:
dsa.removal1: Contain false, misleading, or fraudulent information about an apartment
dsa.removal2: Include discriminatory, offensive, or illegal content
dsa.removal3: Violate third-party rights (e.g., posting without the tenant's authorization)
dsa.removal4: Contain spam, duplicate listings, or commercial advertising unrelated to rental offers
dsa.complaint1: If your content has been removed or restricted, you may submit a complaint to contact@passflat.com within 6 months of the decision.
dsa.complaint2: We will review your complaint and respond within a reasonable time. If you disagree with our decision, you may seek redress through an out-of-court dispute settlement body or the courts.
dsa.complaint3: Users may also report illegal content via contact@passflat.com. We will process reports promptly and inform the reporter of the outcome.
dsa.ranking: Listings are ranked by recency (newest first). Promoted listings — a paid feature — appear at the top of search results for the duration of the promotion. No other algorithmic personalization or profiling is used to order search results.
dsa.contact: For DSA-related inquiries, complaints, or content reports, contact: contact@passflat.com
dsa.odrText: In accordance with EU Regulation 524/2013, consumers may use the European Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform to resolve disputes related to online purchases.

law.title: 11. Governing Law
law.text: These Terms of Service are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Poland. Any disputes arising from these terms shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Warsaw.

contact.title: 12. Contact
contact.text: For questions about these Terms of Service, contact us:
contact.operator: Passflat is operated by Ilya Apaniuk, Warsaw, Poland.

forceMajeure.title: 13. Force Majeure
forceMajeure.text: Passflat shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations due to circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to natural disasters, war, terrorism, pandemics, power outages, internet disruptions, government actions, or third-party service failures.

changes.title: 14. Changes to Terms
changes.text: We may update these Terms of Service. We will notify registered users of significant changes via email at least 14 days before they take effect. For material changes affecting your rights or data processing, we will request your explicit re-acceptance upon next login. If you do not accept the updated terms, you may delete your account. Continued use of the platform after the notification period constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.
